sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (with United States model law influences, particularly Delaware corporate jurisprudence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: None identified as a comprehensive bilateral investment treaty or double taxation agreement currently in force
Compact of Free Association with the United States (economic relations treaty; limited investment protections, does not constitute a BIT/DTAA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (as amended); Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended); Beneficial Ownership (Disclosure) Regulations 2021; Banking Act 1995 (as amended) for regulated financial services.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and identity documents for each UBO, director, and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary public in the UBO's country of citizenship or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing state is not an Apostille Convention member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original certificate of good standing and corporate extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of an authorized bank officer; apostilled if required by RMI registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney executed in favor of the Marshall Islands registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the incorporator's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and the Republic of the Marshall Islands domestic sanctions list. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and PEPs in international organizations, trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD), including source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval for establishing the business relationship, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Threshold and risk rating are aligned with the RMI AMLA and FATF recommendations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations – Online Name Reservation and Clearance System (MI-ROC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in English (Latin script). Names in Marshallese are acceptable but must be transliterated into Latin characters. No foreign scripts are permitted in the registered corporate name. The name must be sufficiently distinguishable from all existing names, and the suffix 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an abbreviation thereof is required. Names must not imply a connection to a government body or regulated activity absent ministerial approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (unless properly used as a corporate suffix)
Stevedoring or Port (requires sectoral license confirmation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Corporations within 14 business days of receipt of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds and any comparative names already approved. The Registrar must render a decision within 10 business days. A further appeal may be lodged with the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days if the Registrar affirms the rejection. During appeal, the name reservation may be held pending judicial review upon payment of a prescribed stay fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office through a licensed registered agent is permissible for satisfying the statutory registered office requirement for a non-resident Business Corporation. However, the actual stevedoring and bulk cargo terminal operations will require physical premises, port authority licenses, and operational permits in the jurisdiction where the marine terminal is located. The Marshall Islands registered office cannot serve as the operational office for stevedoring activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a non-resident offshore business corporation with no physical assets in the Marshall Islands (approximate unannounced inspection risk below 5% annually). If the entity holds a port terminal license or operational assets within the Marshall Islands, the probability rises to 25–40% per annum, and the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit may conduct compliance inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Business Corporations Act (Schedule of Fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee (standard Business Corporation, no minimum capital requirement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Business Corporations Act (Schedule of Fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent acceptance and registered office set-up fee (annual)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident offshore corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO and AML due diligence file processing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk non-resident business corporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille services (estimated for four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and apostille authority in the relevant jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory governmental fee plus prevailing notary tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Verification of source of funds documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance officer / designated financial institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal opinion and corporate record preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate legal counsel in the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee benchmark for non-resident BC formation file

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (Title 50, Marshall Islands Revised Code): §115 (incorporators), §116 (articles of incorporation), §117 (filing and fees), §119 (registered office and agent), §123 (bylaws), §138 (directors), §142 (officers); Marshall Islands Ports Authority Act 1996 (stevedoring license); Environmental Protection Act 1987 (EIA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Justice and Registrar of Corporations, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (approved instrument is the Certificate of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; nominal or zero-par shares permitted; no escrow account or paid-in reserve requirement; subscription consideration may be cash, promissory note, or property and is fixed by the board of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws as filed; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office at Majuro, Marshall Islands, and its registered agent are approved; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the issuance of 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares at US $1.00 par value is authorized; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the directors listed in the consent are elected; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed as officers; FURTHER RESOLVED, that officers are indemnified to the fullest extent permitted by the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; and FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to open bank accounts and execute all stevedoring license applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Online Portal, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Justice and Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RMI online business registry and file a name reservation application containing three ranked corporate name alternatives ending in Corporation, Incorporated, or Limited; pay the US $30 name reservation fee by card; attach the incorporator identification and a sworn declaration that the name is not prohibited, confusing, or deceptively similar; obtain the electronic certificate of name reservation valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Color passport copy of the applicant incorporator
Three ranked corporate name alternatives
Declaration against prohibited or confusing name usage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for confusing similarity, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the Registrar within 5 business days or immediately re-file using a materially distinct name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the Republic of the Marshall Islands; Office of the Registrar of Corporations for form compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation under Section 116 of the Business Corporations Act, specifying the corporate name, registered office street address in Majuro, registered agent consent, authorized share capital, and the corporate purpose which expressly includes bulk port stevedoring, cargo handling, and terminal operations; execute before a notary public and affix notarial stamp.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Consent to serve as registered agent
Certified passport photocopy of incorporator
Landlord consent or proof of street address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice, the incorporator must deliver an executed corrective amendment or amended articles within 7 business days; if the defect relates to notarization, re-notarization and re-submission are required at no additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Justice and Registrar of Corporations (online portal or physical counter, Majuro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation together with the name reservation certificate through the online filing system or at the Registrar counter; pay the US $150 incorporation filing fee and any applicable certified copy charges; retain the electronic payment receipt and filing acknowledgement for follow-up.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation certificate
Government fee payment invoice and receipt
Registered agent acceptance form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for missing fees or inconsistent data, the applicant must reconcile payment or submit a revised filing without prejudice within 5 business days; a written letter of explanation is accepted for minor clerical discrepancies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance; no government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizational meeting of the board; adopt the bylaws; approve the subscription for ordinary shares; elect the initial directors; appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer; approve the registered office and agent; adopt the corporate seal; and authorize the opening of bank accounts by the President.
required_dossiers: Draft Bylaws
Share subscription agreement and contribution proof
Consent to act as director and officer
Minutes of the first Board of Directors meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If unanimity is not achieved, directors may act by unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting under Section 123; unresolved governance disputes are cured by amendment of the bylaws and supplemental written resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate Collection and Regulatory Onboarding for Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (certificate); Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance (TPIN); Majuro Municipal Revenue Office (local business license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download or collect the Certificate of Incorporation after approval; apply to the Revenue and Taxation Office for a Taxpayer Identification Number because the corporation is tax-exempt as a non-resident entity; obtain the municipal business license from the Majuro Revenue Office if any physical office is maintained; notify the Marshall Islands Ports Authority of the corporate status in support of the pending stevedoring license.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Local municipal business license application
Taxpayer Identification Number application form
Notification letter to the Marshall Islands Ports Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, the applicant may request expedited issuance by sworn declaration; a missing or refused municipal business license must be cured by appeal to the Majuro Municipal Revenue Board before physical dock operations commence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Ports Authority (MIPA), Port Licensing Division, Majuro
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Stevedoring and Terminal Operator's License issued under the Marshall Islands Ports Authority Act 1996

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMIEPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A - Full EIA Report mandatory for marine terminal berths, dockside cargo handling infrastructure, and bulk storage areas under the Environmental Protection Act 1987 and RMIEPA review procedures
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to lagoon: pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 10 mg/L, total petroleum hydrocarbons not exceeding 10 mg/L; airborne cargo dust and VOC emissions subject to RMIEPA ambient air standards with no visible fugitive dust beyond terminal boundary; waste handling compliant with MARPOL Annex V through port reception facilities and licensed off-site disposal of oily bilge, hatch-cleaning residues, and stevedoring debris.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Majuro Fire and Emergency Services covering warehouses, conveyor galleries, fuel storage, and office premises; structural load inspection and load-bearing certificate for wharf, mooring bollards, and mobile harbor cranes issued by the Public Works Building Inspector; occupational clearance under RMI workplace health and safety standards covering stevedore gangs, dock equipment lockout procedures, fall protection, and emergency response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Treasury Division (Revenue and Taxation Bureau); official portal: https://www.rmitreasury.net/ and corporate registration portal of the RMI Registrar of Corporations. Customs and excise administration: RMI Customs Service, Ministry of Finance (Majuro).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Business Corporation under the RMI Business Corporations Act 1990 (modeled on Delaware GCL) through the Registrar of Corporations, filing Articles of Incorporation, By-laws, registered office and resident agent in Majuro. Step 2: File Form T-1 (Taxpayer Registration Application) with the RMI Treasury Division to obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation, proof of registered agent, and a statutory declaration that the corporation is a Non-Resident/Business Corporation deriving only foreign-source income. Step 3: If any physical or revenue-generating presence in RMI is contemplated, obtain a business license from the RMI Business License Division and the relevant stevedoring/port operating license from the Marshall Islands Ports Authority (MIPA). Step 4: Register with RMI Customs for import/export declarations. The entire procedure may be completed remotely; no minimum capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone; Territorial_Scope — a Non-Resident Business Corporation (MH_BC) is prima facie outside the RMI tax net. RMI employs a territorial system taxing only income sourced within the RMI. A non-resident corporation with no RMI-source income and no local permanent establishment is not subject to income tax or the 3% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT). Physical stevedoring operations within the Majuro/Ebeye port limits would create RMI-source turnover unless covered by a port concession or statutory exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law contains no check-the-box or US-style entity classification election. Available elections: (a) electing exempt 'Non-Resident Business Corporation' status via Articles/By-laws designation, excluding entitlement to RMI domestic tax privileges in exchange for tax-exempt foreign-source treatment; (b) electing treatment as a Foreign Sales Corporation (FSC) under the RMI Foreign Sales Corporation Act for export trading activities, granting partial GRT/income tax exemptions on foreign trading gross receipts; (c) hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under RMI tax law, but the entity may enter into port concession agreements with MIPA to negotiate escrowed or exempt GRT treatment on terminal stevedoring fees.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — No VAT/GST/Sales-and-Use Tax. Indirect fiscal measures are limited to the RMI Customs Tariff Act 2003 (import duties, ad valorem schedules on imports, excise on fuel/tobacco/alcohol) and the 3% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) on RMI-source business turnover. Exports are generally not subject to duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. For GRT purposes, the registration/filing threshold is US$10,000 in annual gross revenue derived from RMI-source business activity (RMI Income Tax Act 1989, as amended). Non-resident corporations earning only foreign-source revenue are below such threshold and not required to register for GRT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, or digital stamping mandate exists in the RMI. Invoicing is paper-based; customs declarations to RMI Customs are accepted on RMI Customs Declaration forms (manual or scanned/email submission); clearance of exports follows the RMI Customs Tariff Act procedures with no e-invoicing or fiscal data interconnection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — the RMI levies no VAT/GST, so no 0% export VAT rate or refundable input VAT mechanism exists. For indirect tax purposes, goods loaded for export at RMI marine docks are outside the customs import-duty net; no export duty applies to general merchandise. For GRT purposes, stevedoring services performed physically within RMI territorial waters/ports are prima facie RMI-source turnover assessed at 3%, unless (a) the fees are contractually charged to a non-resident vessel owner for offshore transit cargo and no local PE exists, or (b) the operator holds an FSC election or a port concession exemption. Billing, coordination, and managerial services rendered outside the RMI by the non-resident BC are foreign-source and excluded from GRT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Customs Export Declaration (Form CED-1) for controlled or enumerated exports
Ocean/Marine Bill of Lading evidencing export shipment from Majuro or Ebeye port
Dock Receipt and Terminal Manifest issued by the Marshall Islands Ports Authority (MIPA)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export/stevedoring proceeds in foreign currency
Stevedoring Service Agreement and Vessel Call Statement (to substantiate GRT source assessment and foreign-source allocation)
RMI Business License and MIPA Port Terminal Operator's License (regulatory compliance record)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMI maintains no foreign-exchange controls; the 180-day benchmark is a conservative documentation standard (aligned with IRC 994 FSC asset/income guidelines) rather than an RMI statutory deadline. Because no VAT exists, there is no VAT clawback regime. Audits by RMI Treasury may reopen GRT assessments for 3 years (6 years for fraud or omission); penalties for false foreign-source income declarations or improper exemption claims include up to 50% of the tax evaded plus statutory interest, suspension/revocation of the business license, and, under the Customs Tariff Act 2003, seizure and forfeiture of goods, fines up to five times the duty value, and criminal liability for false declarations. RMI Customs additionally may bar the terminal operator or its agent from future export clearances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; the U.S. Federal Reserve acts as the overseas issuer of the official circulating medium (U.S. dollar) by virtue of the Compact of Free Association
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the sole official currency; there is no separate domestic fiat money and, accordingly, no formal exchange-control apparatus. Capital and current account transactions are freely convertible and remittable, including dividends, management fees, and liquidation proceeds, subject only to standard anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) checks. Profits earned by a non-resident Business Corporation may be transferred abroad without Central Bank approval; however, the foreign payee should maintain complete corporate records, board minutes, and supporting invoices to satisfy the carrying bank's compliance review and any U.S. correspondent bank's sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or compulsory conversion rules exist for export receipts in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Stevedoring and port terminal operators may retain proceeds in U.S. dollars or remit them in settlement currencies, provided the associated commercial documentation is retained and all transactions are conducted through a licensed banking institution under the Banking Act 1991, the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act, and the Terrorism and Transnational Organized Crime (Prevention) Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. There is no dedicated e-money institution licensing regime in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Banking Act confines deposit-taking and settlement account maintenance to licensed banks. An offshore digital EMI cannot hold client funds or open settlement accounts without first obtaining a banking license; the Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam act as the primary local clearing points, and their correspondent banking relationships are narrow. Non-bank payments institutions would require special dispensation from the Banking Commissioner, and the likelihood of approval is low for a pure offshore fintech vehicle without a physical office in Majuro.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or an authorised senior officer with signatory rights is normally mandatory for the Bank KYC interview and original document verification at the Majuro branch. Remote opening is possible only on a case-by-case basis where the Banking Commissioner has approved a designated local agent, plus notarised/certified copies of passports, certified corporate documents, and an upfront enhanced due diligence package; the final decision remains discretionary with each bank's compliance committee given the absence of a fully digital onboarding statutory framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt non-resident Business Corporation with no visible local economic activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and good standing certificate, articles of incorporation, registered agent certificate, board resolution authorising account opening, a notarised ownership and control declaration, audited or pro forma financial statements, a detailed stevedoring or port terminal operating plan with anticipated cash flows, and either a valid business licence for the specific port terminal or a legal opinion from Marshall Islands counsel confirming the licence is not required for offshore holding activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or layered ownership structure involving trusts, partnerships, or nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart from ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to signatory, trust deeds or partnership agreements where applicable, UBO declarations with passport copies and source-of-funds letters, nominee service agreements (if any), commercial contracts evidencing the underlying stevedoring operations, and an AML/CFT compliance manual demonstrating nil tolerance for bearer shares and anonymous accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic or sanctions exposure arising from counterparties in port logistics and shipping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed OFAC/politically exposed persons (PEP) screening results for all counterparties, vessel and port call registers, charter parties or terminal service agreements, international trade documents (bills of lading, warehouse receipts, import/export declarations), insurance and freight invoices, and periodic negative-news screening reports prepared by a licensed compliance service provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be executed by SWIFT MT103 credit transfers in U.S. dollars from the ultimate beneficial owner or a regulated financial institution to the beneficiary account held at an RMI-licensed bank. The remitter must use a clearly identified payment purpose code and narrative such as 'Capital Contribution / Increase in Paid-In Capital', referencing the board resolution and the stevedoring project. The receiving bank will verify the source of funds, conduct U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) screening, and confirm that the funds are posted either to the Capital Escrow Account or the Operational Account only after the UBO's beneficial-ownership statement and board resolution have been matched.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements, including payments to port authorities, stevedoring subcontractors, equipment suppliers, and bunker or marine service providers, will be cleared via SWIFT MT103 priority telegraphic transfers, local clearing through Bank of Marshall Islands branch networks, and, for larger capital procurement, through an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) arranged by the RMI bank's correspondent in the United States. Every outgoing payment must be supported by an approved invoice, a purchase order or service contract, a bank-compliant disbursement instruction, and a confirmatory sanctions and denied-party screening certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign exchange forwards (USD against EUR, GBP, JPY, and AUD) with investment-grade counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies where physical delivery is unavailable to the RMI banking sector
Cross-currency swaps (USD against reserve currencies) for long-term port terminal construction loans and equipment leases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Business Corporation (Section 104, Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 October each year, covering the reporting period ending 30 June of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of US$100 or 10% of the unpaid annual fee, whichever is greater; continued non-filing for 90 days may result in administrative dissolution or strike-off, followed by reinstatement costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a non-resident Business Corporation. Independent audit is required only if the entity is listed, subject to maritime regulatory oversight, or specifically directed by the Marshall Islands Ports Authority as a condition of the stevedoring terminal license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting standard prescribed under the Business Corporations Act; IFRS or US GAAP is generally accepted as authoritative practice where financial statements are prepared. Financial statements are not filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public UBO filing. The registered agent must obtain and verify beneficial ownership details and must be notified of any share transfer within 15 days. During the annual compliance review, the agent validates and confirms the current beneficial ownership data; such records remain on file and are available to the Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Net zero income tax jurisdiction; non-resident business corporations are exempt from Marshall Islands income tax. No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions are required because no corporate income tax is imposed at the national level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: MA-BCA Annual Corporation Report and Registration Fee (filed online via the Marshall Islands Registry portal / registered agent)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than the anniversary date of incorporation each year; a 60-day grace period is provided, after which late fees apply

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered corporate name and certificate of incorporation number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent in the Marshall Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the appointed licensed registered agent's name and physical address
State the worldwide principal business address, which may be outside the Marshall Islands
List all directors and officers, including non-resident individuals; no tax residency declaration required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised share capital and issued shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate number of authorised shares and issued shares; no minimum capital requirement
Confirm whether the corporation conducts relevant activity under the Economic Substance Regulations; provide basis of report if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filed annual reports incur a USD 500 late penalty plus USD 100 per month of continued delinquency; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution and loss of limited liability protection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no double tax agreement network and does not impose withholding tax on dividends. Non-resident shareholders are therefore not required to file a tax relief form or submit a tax residence certificate for domestic dividend payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate applies to cross-border royalties and interest as the Marshall Islands does not levy direct or withholding taxes on such income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 (no statutory threshold; no transfer pricing documentation requirement in the Marshall Islands because no corporate income tax is imposed).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Subject to the Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), relevant activities, including transportation and financial activities, require adequate substance in the jurisdiction. Because bulk-port stevedoring involves physical operations, local premises, and employed workers, the economic substance test is satisfied via actual management and operations where the terminal is located. Non-resident holding structures without substance risk being deemed tax-exempt shell companies and subjected to penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Marshall Islands shell corporation to conceal beneficial ownership, artificially transfer profits, or evade home-country taxes without any underlying port operating substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution, remittance of unpaid taxes in foreign jurisdictions, civil penalties of up to USD 10,000 under local corporate law, and criminal fines of USD 25,000 plus imprisonment of up to 5 years in the Marshall Islands for knowingly false filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fraudulent filings; travel bans and restraint orders can be imposed while sanctions and recovery actions are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a nominal port terminal company without real physical assets, local workforce, or identified clients, and using it as an intermediary in round-trip invoicing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Escalated annual registration fees, cancellation of corporate existence, and denial of treaty or tax-exemption benefits; the regulator may publish the entity as lacking substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers face civil claims for misrepresentation, clawback of distributions, and disqualification from serving as directors in any Marshall Islands entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting bulk cargo payments through third-party accounts, laundering proceeds via stevedoring contracts, or failing to keep accurate records of counterparties and cargo transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Marshall Islands Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing framework, fines up to USD 500,000 and terms of imprisonment of up to 10 years for natural persons; corporate license suspension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knows or suspects the laundering arrangement may be prosecuted and held jointly liable for all profits retained through the fraudulent scheme.
